title.narrative: Activity under preparation Modernisation of the Tunisian dispatch centre

description.narrative:
The Tunisian government has set an ambitious objective for its energy transition by aiming to achieve 35 % of the installed capacities of electricity production in the country from renewable energy (RE) sources and to reduce energy demand by 34 % (baseline: 2014) by 2030. Such objectives require, amongst other, a significant investment in RE production as well as investment in the expansion of the electricity transmission and distribution networks. In additional to the expansion of networks needed to connect the consumption and production regions, interconnectors were also deemed necessary to leverage the difference of load duration curves between connected countries to increase RE grid integration.

On 29 June 2007, the Italian and Tunisian governments signed a Joint Declaration that charged Société Tunisienne de l¿Electricité et du Gaz (STEG) and the Italian Transmission System Operator Trasmissione Elettricità Rete Nazionale (TERNA) with developing a project that would interconnect the electricity systems of the two countries. The ELMED project therefore entails the realization of a new bidirectional High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) submarine electricity interconnection and its associated infrastructures between Tunisia (Cap Bon) and Italy (Sicily), with a transmission capacity of 600 MW.

In August 2023, the European Union (EU) has signed a Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) agreement for a EUR 307.6 million grant to implement the project. This is the first time that CEF funds have been assigned to an infrastructure project involving an EU Member State and a third country. The project has been flagged by the EU as part of the European Green Deal, REPowerEU and Global Gateway initiatives and is receiving financing support from Team Europe Initiative financial institutions such as European Investment Bank (EIB), European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), and KfW, in collaboration with the World Bank (WB).

Under the umbrella of ¿ELMED Plus¿, up to EUR 27 million additional EU support is planned to finance further measures deemed essential for the creation of an ecosystem that will allow the ELMED project to meet its objectives. These measures focus on assisting STEG to successfully manage the technical aspects of the project to attain commercial operation on schedule and within budget (Consultancy services for technical and implementation support, EIB-led component). Furthermore, they also improve the framework conditions of the Tunisian energy market by establishing a regulating authority, creating a low carbon pathway and guarantee of origin mechanism (Policy Initiatives Technical Assistance, EBRD-led component). Additionally, the measures envisage a complete modernisation of the Tunisian national Dispatch Center to align the network operations with the foreseen framework conditions improvement and to allow the operationalization of objectives such as energy certification and cross-border energy exchange (Ensuring technological readiness for ELMED by creating a new national dispatch centre, KfW-led component). The latter is subject of this Description of Action.
